run.question:
Alertmanager alert RequestErrorRate (severity warning) is firing for service otel-demo/frontend-proxy since 2026-11-16T16:07:23Z.
Investigate why this alert is firing.

report.summary: The RequestErrorRate alert on otel-demo/frontend-proxy reflects real error spans on frontend-proxy's `ingress` (server) and `router frontend egress` (client) operations. Two distinct error sources are visible. (1) A low-rate background that predates the main fault: 503 responses with envoy flag `UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` on GET /api/products/* and GET /api/recommendations, logged from 15:55:56 onward, whose origin is not established; this is the only error activity visible near the alert's 16:07:23 start. (2) The dominant, still-growing source beginning at 16:16:01: Deployment checkout was rolled out to revision 2 (ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b) with the same image but KAFKA_ADDR changed from kafka:9092 to kafka:9999. The kafka Service (clusterIP 100.66.162.182) exposes only 9092/9093 and the broker listens on 9092, so the new pod's client logs `dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout`, the container exits with code 2 and BackOffs, and the checkout Service is left with zero ready endpoints. Every POST /api/checkout then returns HTTP 500 from frontend, which frontend-proxy surfaces as error spans at ~0.66/s; checkout's own span rate fell to zero. All other 20 pods (including frontend and frontend-proxy, 0 restarts) were Ready, and Kafka itself was healthy, so this is a checkout configuration fault rather than a proxy, frontend or broker outage. The exact alert expression/value (annotation current 1.7333) could not be verified because no Prometheus rules are loaded, so the 16:07:23 firing instant is only partly explained.

claims.text: frontend-proxy's span error series `traces_span_metrics_calls_total{service_name="frontend-proxy",span_name="ingress",status_code="STATUS_CODE_ERROR"}` rose from 0 at 16:16:23 to 0.1222/s at 16:17:23 and 0.663–0.678/s from 16:21:23 to 16:28:23, while the same operation's STATUS_CODE_UNSET rate stayed roughly 11.5–13.2/s, so errors are a real addition to normal traffic.

The same rise appears on frontend-proxy's client operation `router frontend egress` (STATUS_CODE_ERROR 0.664/s at 16:21:23), showing the proxy's upstream call to frontend is what fails, not only its own listener.

frontend's error spans are confined to the checkout path: `POST`, `POST /api/checkout`, `executing api route (pages) /api/checkout` and `grpc.oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder` all reach 0.5185/s at 16:20:23 and 0.663/s at 16:22:23, plus `tcp.connect` errors at 0.0486–0.0741/s from 16:18:23, whereas `/api/cart` operations remain 0.

frontend-proxy's own access log records `POST /api/checkout HTTP/1.1" 500 - via_upstream` for every checkout request from 16:23:39 to 16:24:27 (161 matching lines in 16:20:00–16:24:28, newest 30 all HTTP 500), confirming the 5xx is generated because the `frontend` upstream answered 500.

Deployment checkout was rolled out at 16:16:01: ReplicaSet checkout-849d65649b created (`SuccessfulCreate`), ReplicaSet checkout-5dccddf8bb scaled 1→0 and its pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 deleted, i.e. the whole checkout capacity was replaced.

The two checkout ReplicaSets use the identical image ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.1.3-checkout but different env: revision 1 (checkout-5dccddf8bb, created 15:42:43) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9092, revision 2 (checkout-849d65649b, created 16:16:01) has KAFKA_ADDR=kafka:9999 — a configuration-only change.

Service kafka has clusterIP 100.66.162.182 and exposes only port 9092 (name plaintext) and 9093 (controller); the kafka container is configured with KAFKA_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://:9092,CONTROLLER://:9093 and KAFKA_ADVERTISED_LISTENERS=PLAINTEXT://kafka:9092, so no listener or Service port exists at 9999.

The new checkout container logs repeated `Failed to connect to broker kafka:9999: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout` between 16:19:40 and 16:24:22 and finally `kafka: client has run out of available brokers to talk to: dial tcp 100.66.162.182:9999: i/o timeout`.

Pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz is not Ready (`ContainersNotReady`, ready=false, restartCount 1), its checkout container terminated twice with reason Error and exit code 2 (finishedAt 16:19:39 and 16:23:06), and a Warning `BackOff restarting failed container checkout` was recorded at 16:23:07.

Deployment checkout shows spec.replicas 1 and updatedReplicas 1 but no readyReplicas and no availableReplicas, and Service checkout's Endpoints object contains zero ready addresses with a single notReadyAddress 100.96.4.175 belonging to pod checkout-849d65649b-qqtsz — callers get no backend.

Before the rollout checkout was healthy and produced no STATUS_CODE_ERROR series: `oteldemo.CheckoutService/PlaceOrder`, `orders publish`, `oteldemo.PaymentService/Charge` and related spans ran at about 0.744–0.774/s up to 16:16:23, then decayed (0.3625/s at 16:18:23) and reached exactly 0 from 16:22:23 onward.

frontend-proxy's access log shows a pre-rollout low-rate error pattern unrelated in form to checkout: 14 lines of `503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` on `GET /api/products/*` and `GET /api/recommendations?...` between 15:55:56 and 16:13:31, one further such 503 on `GET /api/cart` at 16:21:59.

Neither the alerting service nor its upstream was down: pods frontend-proxy-6b4d584985-h7j7c and frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv are Running with ready=true, restartCount 0, and frontend-proxy continued to serve 200 responses throughout (thousands of access-log lines, e.g. `POST /api/checkout ... 200` at 16:13:40).

Kafka itself was healthy during the window: pod kafka-ff7884766-ntckh is Running/ready with 0 restarts and its log shows normal KRaft snapshot/segment activity at 16:24:04–16:24:21, and 20 of 21 otel-demo pods (all except the checkout pod) are Running with ready=true and 0 restarts.

Rejected: Kafka broker or its Service is broken, so Kafka clients generally fail. The broker listens on 9092 and the Service publishes 9092, the pod is Ready with no restarts, and only checkout dials the non-existent port 9999; the mismatch is in checkout's env, not in Kafka.

Rejected: frontend-proxy (the alerted service) is itself failing or restarting. Its pod is Ready with 0 restarts and keeps serving 200s; its ERROR spans mirror upstream 500s from frontend on the checkout path, so the proxy is reporting a downstream failure rather than originating one.

The alert's initial firing at 16:07:23, which is 9 minutes before the checkout rollout, was most plausibly triggered by the earlier low-rate 503 `UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination}` responses on frontend's product/recommendation routes (first observed 15:55:56, i.e. matching the first non-zero frontend-proxy error values from ~16:00:23). The resetting upstream (frontend) was Ready with no restarts and its own logs could not be read, so this second error source remains unexplained rather than attributed.

Correct Deployment otel-demo/checkout's pod template so KAFKA_ADDR matches the kafka Service (kafka:9092, the port the broker actually listens on) — or, only if 9999 is intended, add that port to the kafka Service/listener — then let the new ReplicaSet roll and verify checkout-* becomes Ready, the checkout Endpoints gain a ready address, and POST /api/checkout returns 200 again.

Read frontend's application logs (currently returning no lines) and obtain the change record for checkout Deployment revision 2 (the change_history integration is not available in this Run) to identify who changed KAFKA_ADDR and why, and to explain the pre-existing 503 UC resets on product/recommendation routes.

gaps: The RequestErrorRate alerting rule is not available: list_prometheus_rules returned no alert rules (no_data) for rule_name RequestErrorRate and for type=alert, so the rule expression, threshold and the annotation's current value 1.7333 cannot be reproduced; the exact reason the alert transitioned to firing at 16:07:23 is therefore unconfirmed.

Jaeger contained no frontend error traces for 16:10–16:29 (traces_search_by_tags error=true on frontend returned no_data) and frontend-proxy error traces only up to 16:02:52, so the trace-level graph of the checkout failure after the rollout could not be inspected; error-span identity comes from span metrics and access logs only.
frontend pod frontend-675fd7b5c5-n4sbv returned zero log lines from the log endpoint, so the frontend's own error text for the failed PlaceOrder call could not be verified.
frontend-proxy logs were readable only through 16:24:28 (4 MiB read cap), so proxy log evidence for 16:24:28–16:31:14 is unknown.

kube_deployment_status_replicas_ready / kube_deployment_status_replicas_available returned no data for checkout in Prometheus, so deployment readiness in metrics is unknown; the K8s API object state used instead reflects the moment of query, not the incident.

Logs of the pre-rollout checkout pod checkout-5dccddf8bb-9d9c8 are gone (no previous container instances), and the deployment change history integration is not available, so what motivated the 16:16 revision-2 rollout is unknown.

The origin of the 503 UC upstream_reset_before_response_started{connection_termination} responses from frontend is not identified; whether they alone exceeded the (unknown) alert threshold at 16:07:23 is unverified.
next_steps: Fix Deployment otel-demo/checkout KAFKA_ADDR (kafka:9092) or add port 9999 to the kafka Service only if that is the intended design, then confirm the pod becomes Ready and checkout Endpoints gain a ready address.
Pull the change record/audit trail for checkout Deployment revision 2 to identify the actor and intent of the KAFKA_ADDR= kafka:9999 change.
Inspect frontend's Node.js runtime logs (stdout appears empty to the log API) for the connection resets on /api/products and /api/recommendations and for the PlaceOrder gRPC failure message.
Retrieve the RequestErrorRate rule definition from Alertmanager/Prometheus configuration to confirm the expression behind the reported value 1.7333 and the 16:07:23 onset.
